newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks drop on poor demand and Iraq worries.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks drop on poor demand and Iraq worries.

text.p: Jordanian stocks weakened on Monday with minimal institutional support compounded by renewed fears of a U.S. military strike against Baghdad, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index shed 0.25 percent to 143.91 points from 144.27 points on Sunday.
Demand for select bluechips, behind improved trade earlier this week, almost petered out and there was growing selling pressure that undermined the market, dealers said.
The tense situation in northern Iraq worsened sentiment already depressed with few signs of any institutional support to cushion the market from further falls, dealers said.

Jordan's industrial firms still rely on the Iraqi market to export U.N.-permitted items and dealers cited investor jitters over worries over the fate of Iraq's $2 billion oil-for-food deal that would jeopordise the business community's hopes to provide a substantial share of Baghdad's food imports.
Dealers said prices were kept from slipping further by continued select demand on Livestock and Poultry and a handful of industrial stock, but in lesser volumes than the last few days.
LIPO has seen buying interest by an single Gulf-based investor reported to have been gradually building up his stake since last week, some dealers said.
Weak demand on Arab Bank, heavily weighted in the official 60-share index, eroded the market.

The exchange's weakness sent the index below 140 points at the end of June, sliding to levels not reached since 1993, mainly blamed on high interest rates diverting investors to more attractive instruments and minimal institutional support.

A total of 443,580 shares changed hands on Monday in a moderate 634,223 dinar turnover in the cash-squeezed market. Of 46 stocks traded, ten advanced, 29 fell and seven were unchanged. Four posted year lows.

Investment sentiment has been improving since the government announced last week a package of economic reforms in the wake of recent unrest fuelled by the government's doubling of bread prices in line with IMF-agreed economic reforms.
The Pearl Investable Index -- an independent index of the 45 best-performing shares from the official market -- fell 0.23 percent to 80.89 points. It was 15.30 percent down on last year.

In industrials, the leading sector, Jordan Cement Factories shed 20 fils to 3.360 dinars. Dealers said there were no signs of the recent limited foreign buying on the stock in which the government plans to sell part of its majority stake.
Livestock and Poultry rose 10 fils to 600 fils in 80,764 dinar turnover. Dar-al-Dawa rose 50 fils to 4.750 dinars.
In services, Jordan Electric Power was unchanged at 1.540 dinars and National Portfolio shed 20 fils to 1.190 dinars.
In banks, Arab Bank's one dinar fall to 231.000 dinars dragged down the market. Islamic Bank was unchanged at 3.580 dinars.

Industrials dominated on Monday, with a 309,973 dinar turnover and an index drop of 0.13 percent. Banks had a 222,408 dinar turnover and an index drop of 0.35 percent while services had a low 99,591 dinar turnover and an index drop of 0.21 percent.
A total of 178,674 shares worth 113,001 dinars changed hands in thin trade in the parallel market.
